(inferred) Maintaining self-esteem and avoiding the shame of perceived failure in the job search.
(inferred) Financial independence and the ability to pay bills without assistance.
key_facts: The client has applied to many companies but reports receiving no responses.
The client updated their resume's contact information but has not thoroughly reviewed its content.
The client is considering moving transferable skills from the cover letter to the beginning of the resume.

background: An immigrant living far from their family, working hard to support them financially. (inferred) They are separated by over 8000 miles and have not seen their family in three years.
self_view_of_problem: The problem is the sadness and isolation from being far from family during the pandemic, which halted a planned reunion, and the painful reminder during video calls that this distance is necessary to support them.
resistance_drivers: Shifts focus to the therapist's situation when the therapist shares a personal parallel, potentially deflecting from deeper exploration of their own envy and sadness.
Terminates the conversation quickly after expressions of hope or gratitude, avoiding prolonged discussion of emotional pain.

ambivalence.for_change: They want to reunite with their family and bring them to nice places, driven by love and a desire to provide experiences for their aging parents and siblings.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) There is a pull to maintain the current distant, working identity because it fulfills the valued role of family provider, even though it causes sadness.

values_and_stakes: Their role as the hardworking financial provider for their parents and siblings.
The planned future experience of traveling to nice places with their aging family, which represents a core goal and justification for the sacrifice.
(inferred) The stability of their current work and life situation in the new country, which funds the support but requires the distance.
key_facts: They have not seen their family in three years and the pandemic halted a planned visit this year.
Video calls with family simultaneously ease sadness and remind them why they needed to be away.
They envy families who are together during holidays.

background: The client is a student in a community health program, working on a final group project that involves implementing a class in a homeless shelter and measuring its success for the adult male population.
self_view_of_problem: The client frames the problem as being unable to stand working in groups because there is always someone who doesn't pull their own weight, leaving the client to make up for it and causing significant stress.
resistance_drivers: Dismisses therapist's suggestions by stating they have already tried them (e.g., allocating tasks), implying a belief that solutions are ineffective.
Deflects from exploring deeper stress management by quickly agreeing with therapist reassurances without elaboration.

ambivalence.for_change: The client acknowledges feeling a little better after talking and is open to the idea of speaking to the professor, indicating a desire to reduce stress and improve the situation.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) The client may be attached to a self-image as the responsible one who carries the group, fearing that changing the dynamic could threaten their sense of control or identity.

values_and_stakes: Their academic grade (the paper is 50% of their grade).
Their role as the responsible member who ensures the group's success.
(inferred) Their standing with the professor and group members if they escalate concerns.
key_facts: The paper is due in a few days.
The client has already allocated tasks to group members but some still do not stick to the plan.
The client has talked to other group members and most are on board.

background: A person who recently lost their job and is experiencing financial strain, in a 4-year relationship that just ended after an argument about money.
self_view_of_problem: My partner left me after everything I've done, and I'm depressed and losing my sanity because finding a new job is the hardest challenge and I need help with services.
resistance_drivers: Redirects conversation to practical assistance (like government programs) when therapist probes emotional or relational dynamics.
(inferred) Minimizes personal agency in the relationship conflict by framing the breakup as sudden and attributing the problem to external financial issues.

ambivalence.for_change: I'm very motivated to continue my path of success and get help with services to improve my situation.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Changing would require confronting the possibility that my own actions or unemployment contributed to the relationship's end, which threatens my self-view as a good person who did everything.

values_and_stakes: The 4-year relationship with my partner, which has now ended.
(inferred) My identity as a provider and successful person, which is jeopardized by job loss and financial need.
(inferred) Emotional stability and sanity, which I feel I am slowly losing due to the stress.
key_facts: The client lost their job recently and is struggling to find new opportunities.
The breakup argument was triggered by recurring financial issues, with the partner stating the client won't make enough money.
The client was unaware of available support services like those for rent, food, and clothing.

background: (inferred) A college student majoring in biology, taking a heavy course load of 19 credits this semester, who also engages in day trading.
self_view_of_problem: I feel that I will fail a class this semester because I did not study for the last exam, due to taking too many classes (5 classes, 19 credits) and falling behind.
resistance_drivers: Deflects with tangential conversation when therapist offers reassurance or problem-solving strategies (e.g., shifts to discussing the therapist's life or the chat requirement).
Minimizes or dismisses potential solutions presented by the therapist (e.g., contacting professor, grade curves, reviewing materials).

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) A desire to avoid failing the class and the practical consequence of having to retake it.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) An attachment to the identity of being overwhelmed by a tough major and heavy credit load, which serves as an explanation for the problem.

values_and_stakes: Academic progression and not having to retake a difficult professional class.
(inferred) The investment of time and effort already put into the biology major.
(inferred) Maintaining self-reliance and not seeking external academic help (e.g., from the professor).
key_facts: The client took their last exam last week and feels they will fail it.
The client did not study for this exam because they were taking 5 classes (19 credits) and was falling behind.
The client states the professor will not release grades until the end of the week and does not teach in the winter, limiting immediate recourse.

background: (inferred) A parent staying home with children during the pandemic, previously employed outside the home.
self_view_of_problem: Staying home with my children instead of going to work is making me anxious, and it feels like all I do is wait on them with no days off.
resistance_drivers: (inferred) Dismisses or deflects practical suggestions for external support (e.g., community assistance) with brief acknowledgment but no commitment.
(inferred) Focuses on external, immutable constraints (pandemic, lack of paycheck) as barriers to change, rather than internal or actionable factors.

ambivalence.for_change: I really do need to find a way to have some personal space once in awhile.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Feels that the role of being the sole, constant caregiver is an inescapable and defining obligation, making change seem impossible.

values_and_stakes: The role and identity of being the primary, responsible caregiver for her children.
The financial security and sense of appreciation tied to her previous paycheck and work role.
(inferred) The stability and routine of her family's daily life, which could be disrupted by seeking outside help or personal time.
key_facts: She explicitly states that staying home with her children instead of going to work is making her anxious.
She feels overwhelmed because there are no days off on the horizon.
She had not considered looking into community help for assistance.

background: (inferred) The client is an adult experiencing significant depression, likely unemployed or on leave due to their symptoms, with a social circle that includes people who notice and judge their condition.
self_view_of_problem: I can't live a regular life like 'healthy' people do because my mind is my enemy, leaving me with no interest or motivation to do anything, which is embarrassing when others notice my symptoms.
resistance_drivers: Terminates or attempts to terminate the conversation when feeling tired or overwhelmed, as seen with 'I have to go now' and later agreeing to stay only briefly.
Uses avoidance as a primary coping strategy, explicitly stating they stay away from mean people and stop trying to explain symptoms to others who won't understand.
(inferred) Demonstrates passive engagement by providing minimal, factual answers to direct questions (e.g., sleep duration) without elaboration or seeking further help.

ambivalence.for_change: I go to all my therapy appointments and try to participate, indicating a commitment to seeking help.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Changing would mean confronting the shame and exposure of having others notice my symptoms, which feels more threatening than the current isolation.

values_and_stakes: The ability to appear 'normal' and avoid embarrassment in front of others who notice my symptoms.
The safety and control found in avoiding 'mean people' and explanations that lead to misunderstanding.
(inferred) The identity of being someone who is fundamentally different from 'healthy' people, which provides a rationale for my struggles.
key_facts: The client sleeps about 3 broken hours a night.
The client knows all the sleep hygiene rules but states 'My mind just wont rest'.
The client feels ashamed that they are not like other people who can complete things like hygiene care without a struggle.

background: (inferred) A young adult woman who was in a long-term relationship and was planning to move in with her boyfriend before the breakup.
self_view_of_problem: She sees the problem as her boyfriend betraying her by cheating with his best friend for three months, which has left her unable to eat or sleep and feeling like she has to start all over.
resistance_drivers: Deflects practical advice by focusing on the emotional pain and loss (e.g., responding to suggestions about self-care or friends by emphasizing how hard it is when everything reminds her of him).
Expresses disbelief and hurt when confronted with the reality that he doesn't love her, questioning how love and betrayal can coexist.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) She wants to feel better and acknowledges she needs to eat and sleep, indicating a pull toward self-preservation.
ambivalence.against_change: She is pulled away from change by the emotional attachment to the relationship and the identity threat of starting over, which feels overwhelming and unfair.

values_and_stakes: The three-year relationship and shared future plans, including moving in together next year.
Her sense of security and trust, which was shattered by the betrayal with someone she was told not to worry about.
(inferred) Her social support system, as she indicates he was her everything and she has no friends to talk to.
key_facts: She confirmed the cheating by noticing signs and confronting him, and he admitted it without remorse.
She has not been able to eat or sleep for a few days since the breakup.
She states she has no friends to talk to because he was her everything.

background: (inferred) A student in higher education, likely college or university, taking courses in political science, government, history, economics, biology, physics, and math.
self_view_of_problem: I can't figure out a good strategy to study for my tests, mainly the ones that require memorization.
resistance_drivers: Dismisses or minimizes suggested solutions by immediately citing external complications (e.g., online group study being less effective due to COVID).
(inferred) Shows passive acceptance ('Yes, I could. It brings its own complications but it should be fine.') rather than active engagement, indicating a reluctance to fully commit to new strategies.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) I want to pass my tests and stop failing, so I need to find an effective study method.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Changing my study habits feels daunting and unfamiliar, and I am attached to the comfort of my current, though ineffective, approach.

values_and_stakes: Academic success and passing grades in memorization-heavy subjects.
(inferred) The efficiency and social support previously gained from in-person study groups.
(inferred) Personal competence and self-image as a capable student.
key_facts: The client fails tests primarily in subjects requiring memorization (political science, government, history, economics, biology).
The client states online group studying is 'no longer as effective' since classes moved online due to COVID.
The client has tried group studying before and found it 'kind of working for a while'.

background: (inferred) A small business owner who crafts and sells wreaths and tumblers, currently trying to expand their crafting business.
self_view_of_problem: I need more motivation, time, and energy to get my business moving and be more serious about it.
resistance_drivers: (inferred) Deflects practical suggestions by reframing the problem as a lack of personal resources (motivation, time, energy) rather than exploring external solutions.
(inferred) Minimizes past business efforts ('did not have time to be as serious') to justify current struggles without examining deeper barriers.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) Wants to 'kick it up and get things moving' and be more serious, indicating a desire for growth and success.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Feels overwhelmed by the demands of expansion, fearing that increased seriousness will require more resources than they possess.

values_and_stakes: The success and viability of their crafting business.
(inferred) Their identity as an independent, self-sufficient craftsperson and business owner.
(inferred) The personal satisfaction and financial stability derived from growing their own venture.
key_facts: The client is switching product focus from wreaths to tumblers due to easier storage.
The client has sold wreaths for a while but not in a serious, high-volume capacity previously.
The client has not looked into organizations that help small business owners.

background: A person with a severe autoimmune disorder (Ulcerative Colitis) for eight years, on immunosuppressant medications, facing possible major surgery. They are married with two children, an 8.5-year-old and a one-year-old.
self_view_of_problem: The problem is a 'crazy,' unpredictable, and depressing health condition that is worsened by stress and the pandemic, and is compounded by feeling misunderstood, especially by her husband.
resistance_drivers: Deflects from exploring her own emotional responses by immediately pivoting to external stressors (like the pandemic or her husband's behavior) when anxiety is acknowledged.
(inferred) Minimizes the depth of her own distress or need for personal coping strategies by emphasizing external validation ('people really don't understand') as the primary unmet need.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) She desires relief from the anxiety and depression caused by her illness's unpredictability and the feeling of being a burden or failing her children.
ambivalence.against_change: She is attached to the identity of being the strong, misunderstood patient who must endure an unpredictable condition that others cannot truly comprehend.

values_and_stakes: Her role as a capable and present mother to her two children, especially feeling she 'fail[s] them a lot'.
Her marital relationship, which provides practical partnership but where understanding and emotional support feel absent.
Her sense of control and predictability in managing a chronic, 'forever changing' illness.
key_facts: She has been hospitalized 'so many times its crazy' over eight years of illness.
Her husband was present for a doctor's grave prognosis and an emergency blood transfusion but remained emotionally unreadable and unresponsive.
She describes her youngest child as a 'miracle baby' born while she was on birth control, indicating a deep value placed on her children despite her illness.

background: A person going through a divorce after their wife cheated, currently staying with family out of state. (inferred) They previously enjoyed crafting and selling items on Etsy.
self_view_of_problem: The problem is that his wife cheated, wants a divorce, and has blocked all communication, leaving him unable to eat, sleep, or function due to anxiety and anger.
resistance_drivers: Deflects from self-examination by focusing on the wife's actions and moral failings (e.g., questioning why people get married if they'll look elsewhere).
Expresses a wish for an external solution ('secret') to stop loving her, rather than engaging with the internal work of moving on.
(inferred) Resists behavioral activation by stating it's easier to stay in bed and do nothing, despite acknowledging the need for distraction.

ambivalence.for_change: He wants to stop loving his wife and find relief from his debilitating anxiety and insomnia.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Holding onto his love and attachment to his wife feels integral to his identity and the history of the marriage, making letting go a threat to his sense of self.

values_and_stakes: The marriage itself and the life he built with his wife.
His ability to function in daily life (eating, sleeping, getting up).
His previous creative identity and enjoyment derived from crafting and selling on Etsy.
key_facts: His wife has blocked him on all communication channels and is cohabiting with the new partner.
He is physically separated, staying with family out of state.
The new partner answers his wife's phone and 'talks trash' to him.

background: A man recently married earlier this year, now going through a divorce because his wife is cheating; he has returned to his home state to stay with his family.
self_view_of_problem: He frames the problem as being unable to let his wife go in his head and heart, consumed by thoughts of her despite her infidelity and rejection.
resistance_drivers: Deflects from his own agency by focusing on external factors (wife's potential drug use, the other woman controlling her phone) when confronted with the need to move on.
Minimizes his own emotional dependency by labeling himself as 'weak' while simultaneously expressing an inability to let go, creating a self-defeating loop.
(inferred) Resists accepting finality by holding onto hope for reconciliation (e.g., hoping she regrets her decision) when faced with evidence the marriage is over.

ambivalence.for_change: He explicitly states 'I want to let her go' and is talking to someone new who wants to pursue him.
ambivalence.against_change: He feels a deep emotional attachment and love for his wife, fearing that letting go would mean abandoning his commitment to be 'in it till the end'.

values_and_stakes: His identity as a committed husband who honors marriage vows ('I would of never married her if I wasn't in it till the end').
The specific relationship with his wife, which he still loves and hopes to salvage.
(inferred) His self-respect and sense of being a non-'weak' person, which is threatened by his continued attachment.
key_facts: His wife has blocked him on all social media and his phone number, and has another woman answering her phone.
He has already returned to his home state and is staying with his family.
He is already talking to someone new who knows about his feelings for his wife and wants to pursue him.

background: (inferred) The client is employed and has a family, as they mention focusing on 'myself and my family' and discuss workplace dynamics.
self_view_of_problem: The client frames the problem as feeling unliked and uncared for at work, where they put in effort to help and be nice but others are dismissive and take advantage without reciprocating.
resistance_drivers: Shifts to a self-protective withdrawal ('just keep to myself') when feeling hurt by lack of reciprocity.
Adopts a transactional stance ('treat people as they treat me') when therapist advises maintaining kindness without expectation.

ambivalence.for_change: The client wants to learn to say no and set boundaries without guilt to stop feeling taken advantage of.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) The client fears losing the identity of being a helpful, kind person if they stop going out of their way for others.

values_and_stakes: The role of being a kind, helpful person at work, which they derive self-worth from.
The hope for reciprocal friendships with coworkers, which feels at risk if they stop initiating.
(inferred) Family harmony, as they plan to redirect focus there, implying current work stress affects it.
key_facts: The client feels coworkers are dismissive when they try to talk and expect help without appreciation.
The client has been going out of their way to help people and remember birthdays.
The holidays make it harder for the client to set boundaries.

background: Works in a team environment with a new supervisor and peers they care about. (inferred) Has applied for another job within the same company.
self_view_of_problem: My new supervisor hates me and has made a personal goal to inhibit my ability to do my job by taking away all the parts I value, crushing my spirit and making me and my team miserable with no recourse.
resistance_drivers: Deflects from actionable solutions (like a formal complaint) by emphasizing systemic hopelessness (e.g., 'no recourse,' next manager is 'awful').
Expresses passive hope ('waiting for someone to notice,' 'hoping she fails') instead of initiating direct action, until explicitly encouraged by the therapist.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) I desire to escape the misery and exhaustion and regain a sense of agency and purpose in my work.
ambivalence.against_change: Feels a protective loyalty and responsibility toward my peers, making change feel like abandoning them.

values_and_stakes: My role as a supportive and helpful leader to my team peers.
The specific, valued parts of my job that I loved and that gave my work meaning.
(inferred) My professional identity as a competent and valued employee within this company.
key_facts: The client has already applied for another job within the company and there is interest in them.
The client is the person their team expects to help with tasks the supervisor is not performing.
The client plans to gather notes from peers to build a viable anonymous complaint.

background: (inferred) A student who has borrowed books from their school library and is facing a financial and administrative burden due to losing them.
self_view_of_problem: I lost those books, I cannot even explain how it happen, and now I need to find almost 3 thousand dollars to replace them, which is too painful and giving me a headache.
resistance_drivers: Shifts focus to external blame (e.g., school not listening) when pressed for personal accountability or solutions.
Uses vague, distressed language ('it is a fucking thing') to avoid concrete planning or self-examination when therapist probes for details.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) I want to find the books or resolve the debt to relieve my pain and headache.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) I am attached to avoiding full responsibility and the shame of admitting my carelessness caused this loss.

values_and_stakes: Financial stability (owing ~$3000 for the lost books).
Academic standing and relationship with the school/library.
(inferred) Personal integrity and self-image as a responsible borrower.
key_facts: The client lost 5 borrowed library books, with one priced at $1000, totaling nearly $3000.
The client packed the books in one bag and suspects someone may have carried it away or they misplaced it.
The client plans to check the CCTV of their room and look around for the books.

background: An adult with a spouse and children who has accepted a new, well-paying job in California, while his extended family (parents, siblings, friends) all live in Washington. (inferred)
self_view_of_problem: I have anxiety to leave my families. I need to take care of my mother and monitor my young ones, and they will definitely need me.
resistance_drivers: Rejects alternatives when they threaten his core identity as the primary caregiver (e.g., says 'NO' to therapist suggesting siblings help, dismisses organizations).
Focuses on concrete, unsolvable emotional dependencies (e.g., 'she feels more happy while seeing me') to counter logical solutions.

ambivalence.for_change: The job gets a big cash, providing financial security for his immediate family.
ambivalence.against_change: Fear that his essential role and identity as the indispensable son and caregiver will be invalidated or proven unnecessary.

values_and_stakes: His role as his mother's primary source of happiness and care.
His immediate family's (wife and children) financial security and future.
(inferred) His sense of control and certainty in his family's well-being.
key_facts: He states his mother will not leave his father, implying a fixed care situation.
He does not know anybody in California, predicting social isolation concerns.
He is not sure his siblings are committed enough to care for his parents, predicting distrust in shared responsibility.

background: (inferred) A parent of a 4th-grade child, managing the child's education during a period of remote learning and teacher absence.
self_view_of_problem: My child is falling behind in school because he has a good heart but just doesn't like school, and I'm trying to figure out where the line is between helping him and not upsetting him.
resistance_drivers: Deflects by shifting focus to the therapist's personal experience when asked about concrete actions (e.g., asking 'Do you have children?').
Expresses hesitation about implementing known solutions due to external circumstances (e.g., tutors during COVID-19).
Minimizes the problem's severity by affirming the child will be okay while simultaneously expressing worry.

ambivalence.for_change: I think I just need to be more firm with him and put on my big boy pants and deal with it.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) I fear that pushing for change will trigger his frustration and lead to huge blow-ups and fights, which I want to avoid.

values_and_stakes: A peaceful, conflict-free relationship with his child, avoiding huge blow-ups and fights.
The child's emotional well-being and self-esteem, as he has a good heart and gets frustrated when pushed.
(inferred) His perceived competence and identity as a supportive, effective parent who can navigate remote learning and teacher absence.
key_facts: He has already bribed his child with a video game for acing upcoming tests.
His child's current teacher is out with a medical condition, complicating remote learning.
Tutors have helped in the past, but he is unsure about using one now due to COVID-19.

background: (inferred) A person with a family and young children, navigating remote learning and social distancing during the COVID-19 pandemic.
self_view_of_problem: I'm worried I'm not getting to see my friends enough, which is causing me to be impatient and short with my family, and I worry we are drifting apart.
resistance_drivers: Deflects by attributing stress to external circumstances like remote learning when discussing emotional impact.
Uses self-labeling ('I'm pretty introverted') to minimize the initial significance of the problem.
Expresses a desire for more connection but immediately cites practical barriers (kids, safety) without exploring solutions until prompted.

ambivalence.for_change: I want more time with my friends and feel better after making a plan to call them.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Fear that initiating contact might be burdensome to busy friends or disrupt an established, low-effort dynamic.

values_and_stakes: The quality and closeness of specific friendships she feels are drifting apart.
Her role and harmony within her family, as her impatience affects them.
(inferred) Her identity as a responsible parent protecting her children's health from COVID-19.
key_facts: She interacts with friends mostly by text and zooms about once a week.
She has met friends a few times, outside and socially distanced.
She has not talked to her friends about how they are feeling regarding the drifting apart.

background: (inferred) An individual living alone, likely older or with underlying health conditions, who is under strict isolation due to being at high risk from Covid-19.
self_view_of_problem: I am depressed about Covid and being restricted from going places. I feel very isolated, alone, and helpless, like I am stuck at home with a feeling of doom and can't contribute to anyone.
resistance_drivers: Minimizes own suffering by comparing it to perceived advantages ('I have a good life and have my health so I feel guilty for complaining').
Withholds expressing negative feelings to avoid being perceived as a burden ('I hate feeling like I am a debbie downer type. I do not want to tell anyone how I feel.').

ambivalence.for_change: I want to reach out online and find a group to join to help my mood.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) A fear that reaching out will confirm feelings of being a burden or 'debbie downer' to others.

values_and_stakes: The ability to contribute to and lend a hand to other people.
A sense of purpose and accomplishment in daily life.
(inferred) Maintaining a self-image as someone who is resilient and does not complain despite having a 'good life'.
key_facts: Client has not been able to eat or clean their house and just lays around with no energy.
Client immediately plans to act on the therapist's suggestion by going on Facebook after the session.
Client felt understood and validated by the therapist, which they had not felt in a long time.

background: A married father of two kids living in Chicago, who works in a professional environment where he deals with increasing power and office politics. (inferred)
self_view_of_problem: I am worried that COVID-19 has made me depressed, making me impatient and sadder than normal, and I am also worried that I am not playing the political game well enough for the career growth I want.
resistance_drivers: Deflects by asking the therapist about their personal coping methods when his own behaviors (like increased drinking) are implicitly challenged.
Minimizes the scope of his problem by focusing on maintained positive habits (like not missing a workout) when broader negative trends are discussed.

ambivalence.for_change: I want to alleviate my sadness, impatience, and depression to feel better and advance my career.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Changing my straightforward approach to office politics feels like a threat to my authentic self and well-mannered identity.

values_and_stakes: My career growth and advancement potential are at risk if I don't engage more effectively with office politics.
My role as a stable, well-mannered father and husband is at risk if my depression and impatience worsen.
My personal health and grounding routine (daily workouts, monthly hikes) are at risk if stress and drinking increase.
key_facts: He reports drinking more than he wants to since COVID-19 started.
He has not missed a workout since COVID-19 started.
He lives across the street from a forest preserve, which he calls a 'life saver'.

background: Client lost their dream job during the pandemic, now works a lower-paying job, gained weight while working from home, and recently moved into a new apartment complex.
self_view_of_problem: I have been feeling down and depressed every day for months, mainly due to self-esteem issues, and it's hard to convince myself things will get better soon.
resistance_drivers: Deflects by shifting focus to the therapist's experiences when asked to commit to a specific action (e.g., asking therapist about exercise class after suggestion).
Expresses helplessness or lack of knowledge about how to begin when a concrete step is suggested (e.g., 'It's hard to take the first steps. I don't even know where to begin.').

ambivalence.for_change: I feel like I have a bunch of new ideas to start feeling better.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) There is an emotional attachment to a passive, hopeless identity where external circumstances are to blame, making active change feel overwhelming and futile.

values_and_stakes: Financial stability and a better job are at risk if change requires uncertain steps or commitments.
The comforting, low-demand companionship of their cat is at risk if change requires more energy or social engagement.
(inferred) The safety of isolation and familiar routines is at risk if change involves social exposure with new neighbors or volunteers.
key_facts: Client gained a lot of weight while working from home.
Client recently moved into a new apartment complex a couple weeks ago.
Client knows a lot of food banks around them are in need of volunteers.

background: A person living in Washington with their spouse and children, who has family (parents, siblings) and friends in Washington, and has been offered a new job in California.
self_view_of_problem: I am scared to leave my town and my family, and I'm anxious and worried about who I will socialize with and how I will monitor my children if I take this new job in California.
resistance_drivers: Repeats the list of family and friends in Washington when the therapist acknowledges anxiety, suggesting a pattern of reiterating emotional attachments to counter the push toward change.

Immediately questions the decision ('or should i not take the job?', 'Or I should forgo the job') when the benefits are mentioned, showing a trigger of considering abandonment of the opportunity when faced with its advantages.

ambivalence.for_change: I acknowledge the job entails good cash and would benefit my family.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) I am attached to my daily routines and identity as a present family member and community figure in Washington, and leaving threatens that sense of self and belonging.

values_and_stakes: Daily, in-person contact with my mother and the ability to monitor my young children.
My established social network of friends and extended family in Washington for companionship and support.
The stability and familiarity of my current town and community life.
key_facts: The client sees their mother every day.
The client has a wife and children who would move with them.
The client states they have nobody in California.

background: An IT consultant who recently lost their job and is struggling to pay bills, currently doing some part-time freelance work but with savings running out.
self_view_of_problem: The client frames the problem as a financial and emotional crisis caused by job loss, stating 'emotionally it is hard to cope' and 'my emotion is getting worse and worse. Stress I guess.'
resistance_drivers: Deflects practical suggestions by focusing on financial or logistical barriers (e.g., questioning the pay of delivery work, citing cost of therapy).
Minimizes the severity of their emotional distress to avoid seeking help (e.g., implies charities only help if suicidal, not for 'stress from normal job seekers').

ambivalence.for_change: They express a desire for advice and are willing to take any job, including outside their field, to improve their situation.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) There is an emotional pull toward maintaining self-reliance and avoiding the perceived stigma or inadequacy of accepting lower-status work or charity.

values_and_stakes: Financial independence and the ability to pay bills without relying on savings or external aid.
Professional identity and status as an IT consultant, which is at risk if they take temporary, lower-skilled work.
(inferred) Personal dignity and self-sufficiency, threatened by the prospect of needing food banks or charitable counseling.
key_facts: The client's savings are running out despite some freelance work.
The client has not yet sought help from food banks or charitable counseling services.
The client works in IT consulting but is willing to take any job temporarily, including food delivery.

background: A woman who was in a five-year relationship that recently ended due to her partner's infidelity, and who expresses a strong desire to have children.
self_view_of_problem: She frames the problem as being unable to stop crying and feeling depressed about being alone after the breakup, and sees herself as having wasted five years on a relationship that didn't lead to marriage and children.
resistance_drivers: Deflects from therapist's positive reframing by immediately returning to her sense of loss and wasted time.
Expresses difficulty envisioning a positive future, focusing instead on the immediate pain and what she could have had.

ambivalence.for_change: She acknowledges that she cannot be with someone she doesn't trust and that she has learned about her own standards for respect and appreciation.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) She is emotionally attached to the future she imagined with her ex-partner, including marriage and children, and letting go of that vision feels like a profound loss.

values_and_stakes: The opportunity to have children, which feels jeopardized by the end of the relationship.
Her self-respect and the standard of being valued and appreciated in a committed relationship.
(inferred) Her identity as a future wife and mother, which was tied to this long-term relationship.
key_facts: She broke up with her boyfriend after discovering he was cheating, despite him having 'always been so good' to her.
The relationship lasted five years and she wanted to get married, but he never asked.
She loves boating and painting but had not engaged in these hobbies in years due to being 'wrapped up in drama' with her ex.

background: (inferred) A working adult whose hours and pay have been reduced due to the coronavirus pandemic, carrying significant student loan debt.
self_view_of_problem: I feel stuck due to job stuff and the pandemic, worried about the future, a reduction in hours and less pay.
resistance_drivers: Expresses uncertainty and self-doubt when considering new actions (e.g., 'not sure where to start' or 'if i am qualified').
Immediately cites a concrete obstacle (student loan debt) when a potential solution (certifications) is introduced.

ambivalence.for_change: I should definitely look into certifications and try not to get down, acknowledging a need to research and educate myself.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Fear that taking action to improve my situation will lead to more financial burden and risk, given my existing student loan debt.

values_and_stakes: Financial stability and avoiding additional debt.
(inferred) A sense of security and predictability in my current employment role, even if it is reduced.
key_facts: The client is carrying significant student loan debt.
The client's work hours and pay have been reduced due to the pandemic.
The client has considered looking for other employment but feels unsure how to start.

background: A self-employed writer who writes about movies and short stories, and has a pacemaker.
self_view_of_problem: Life is just bad and sad, a bad year, with scary political turmoil and not working a lot.
resistance_drivers: Deflects from personal problems by focusing on external events like politics and the virus.
Minimizes their own struggles and capabilities, e.g., 'i'm horrible at doing things for others'.
(inferred) Avoids discussing deeper emotional pain by engaging in tangential, practical topics like writing platforms.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) Wants to feel better and be more productive, as shown by interest in earning money through writing.
ambivalence.against_change: Feels attached to a self-view as someone who is 'horrible at doing things for others' and must be paid to 'do my thing'.

values_and_stakes: The identity and autonomy of being a self-employed writer who only does 'my thing'.
(inferred) The safety and familiarity of their current, low-work routine and isolation.
(inferred) The integrity of their creative output, which might be compromised by commercial pressures.
key_facts: The client quit their job last year because of mental health.
The client is self-employed but states 'not working alot'.
The client has a pacemaker.

background: Works at a small company of 13 people, is high enough in the company to see internal financial numbers. (inferred) Likely in a professional or managerial role given their access to business performance data.
self_view_of_problem: Frames the problem as being 'bummed' and worn down by an unfair pay cut, because he sees the company's numbers are good and improving, making the cut seem unjustified rather than necessary.
resistance_drivers: Deflects from direct action by shifting focus to external validation or the therapist's situation, as seen when asked about discussing the issue at work.
(inferred) Minimizes his own agency by emphasizing external barriers like a tough job market when considering change.

ambivalence.for_change: Admits the pay cut might be a needed 'catalyst' for a career change he's been considering for a long time.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Feels a pull toward staying due to familiarity, his insider knowledge of the company, and the risk of leaving a known, improving situation for an uncertain job market.

values_and_stakes: His current professional role and insider status at a small, improving company.
Financial stability and salary level, which is currently at risk due to the cut.
(inferred) A sense of fairness and trust in leadership, which is damaged by the perceived dishonesty about the company's performance.
key_facts: He has already started looking for a new job but finds it hard because 'there isn't much open'.
He has only discussed the pay cut with one coworker, who has since quit.
He sees concrete financial data showing the company is on pace to do better this year and next.

background: A person who has worked in bars, cafes, and restaurants their entire life, currently living with their elderly grandmother and mother, and has a daughter in virtual school.
self_view_of_problem: I am struggling so bad finding a job because I am scared of Covid 19, and I have never been this broke and poor in my life.
resistance_drivers: Expresses self-doubt about capability when new options (online work) are suggested, framing it as being 'way out my league'.
Shifts focus from the proposed solution to logistical obstacles (managing work while daughter is in virtual school) after showing initial optimism.

ambivalence.for_change: I need to work right now, my bills are piling up, and I don't want my family to have to support me.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Fear that taking any outside job will endanger the health of my vulnerable grandmother and mother.

values_and_stakes: The physical safety and health of my elderly grandmother and mother.
Financial independence and avoiding being a burden on my family.
(inferred) My identity and self-efficacy as a skilled worker in the food and beverage industry.
key_facts: The client has worked exclusively in bars, cafes, and restaurants their entire career.
The client lives with two elderly or health-compromised family members.
The client has a daughter who is in virtual school.

background: (inferred) A parent of five children, currently experiencing financial strain.
self_view_of_problem: I don't have enough money to buy my kids Christmas gifts, and they are expecting toys from Santa.
resistance_drivers: Immediately dismisses a suggested solution (homemade gifts) by stating a personal inability ('I cannot craft').
Shifts focus from the core emotional problem (feeling inadequate) to a logistical request for specific craft ideas.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) I want to find a way to give my children a happy Christmas despite the financial constraints.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Changing my approach to gift-giving threatens my identity as a provider who meets my children's material expectations.

values_and_stakes: The expectation and happiness of her five children during Christmas.
Her role as a parent who provides and fulfills promises (like Santa bringing toys).
key_facts: The client has five children.
The client initially stated she cannot craft.
The client latched onto the specific idea of a painted cardboard box fort after the therapist suggested it.

background: A college student taking an evening course via distance learning during the pandemic, living in an apartment.
self_view_of_problem: The problem is a stressful technological and logistical challenge: trying to concentrate while following an Excel class on a tiny phone screen, needing to switch between applications, and dealing with disruptive classmates.
resistance_drivers: Focuses on external, logistical barriers (like screen size and mute issues) when discussing the core stress of the class.
Shifts conversation to the therapist's personal life and solutions when anxiety symptoms are mentioned.
Expresses attraction to idealized, minimalist tech solutions (like a portable monitor) that align with a self-image of portability, potentially avoiding deeper engagement with the anxiety.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) A desire to reduce the physical symptoms of anxiety (pounding ears, heartbeat) and improve concentration to succeed in the course.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) An attachment to a self-concept of being minimalist and portable, which might conflict with implementing more permanent or cumbersome solutions.

values_and_stakes: Academic performance and grades in the college course.
(inferred) A personal identity centered on portability, minimalism, and the ability to work from anywhere.
Financial resources, as indicated by seeking a good deal on Amazon for a potential solution.
key_facts: Client experiences physical anxiety symptoms (pounding ears, inability to hear) during class, especially with headphones.
Client has a laptop and a large TV available, suggesting a potential hardware solution is physically possible.
Client has already researched specific tech products like portable second monitor screens for laptops.

background: (inferred) An adult living through the COVID-19 pandemic, likely with a job and social network, who identifies as an introvert and enjoys reading and movies.
self_view_of_problem: COVID-19 has me needing people more, but I'm an introvert and want to go out but can't, leading to lonely feelings.
resistance_drivers: Deflects by asking the therapist questions about their own experiences when prompted for personal action or reflection.
Minimizes the effectiveness of suggested coping strategies (e.g., Zoom, virtual museum tours) by stating they are 'not great' or already done.
(inferred) Avoids deep exploration of personal emotional struggles by keeping conversation focused on shared, surface-level interests like books and movies.

ambivalence.for_change: I want to go out and be around other people to alleviate lonely feelings caused by the pandemic.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Changing my introverted habits and routines to seek more social connection feels uncomfortable and threatens my established identity and comfort zone.

values_and_stakes: My established identity as an introvert, which provides comfort and predictability.
My personal routines and habits that structure my daily life.
(inferred) My sense of independence and self-sufficiency, which might be compromised by admitting a strong need for others.
key_facts: The client previously used reading Harry Potter as an alternative to a lifestyle of drinking and late nights.
The client has already tried Zoom calls and virtual museum tours but finds them insufficient.
The client is considering going to the park or walking on trails as a potential new activity.

background: (inferred) The client is a manager or supervisor in a workplace, responsible for employees and reporting to a higher-level supervisor.
self_view_of_problem: The client frames the problem as an employee gossiping and seeking the attention of their bosses, which is hurtful and has unexpectedly hurt their ego.
resistance_drivers: (inferred) Avoids direct confrontation by delaying action (e.g., hasn't asked supervisor yet, plans to 'think about it').
(inferred) Seeks external validation and guidance rather than asserting their own managerial authority.

ambivalence.for_change: The client feels stressed and hurt by the situation and wants to resolve it to reduce emotional distress.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) The client's ego is invested in not appearing affected, creating a pull to avoid actions that might expose vulnerability.

values_and_stakes: Their professional authority and respect as a manager.
Their relationship with their supervisor and perceived competence.
(inferred) Their self-image as someone not usually hurt by workplace dynamics.
key_facts: The client's employee has been relaying messages from the supervisor, which the supervisor should have communicated directly.
The client has not yet spoken to their supervisor about the situation, though they plan to.
The client states their ego is getting hurt by this, which they say usually doesn't happen.

background: An introverted person who works from home most of the week but goes into an empty office building 1-2 days per week, has a child engaged in remote learning, and owns a dog. (inferred)
self_view_of_problem: I am having a difficult time not being able to go out, finding myself short and impatient, and I miss the social aspects, mostly my friends.
resistance_drivers: Minimizes the significance of social connections when prompted ('Who I didnt see a ton anyways').
Deflects from exploring emotional needs by shifting focus to practical routines or the therapist's experience ('have you tried anything that helps?').

ambivalence.for_change: I would like to just go out and have a drink at a bar, and I think going to the park with someone sounds like a wonderful idea.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) There is a pull to maintain the self-sufficient, routine-driven identity of an introvert who 'has always' coped with exercise alone, making social outreach feel unnecessary or burdensome.

values_and_stakes: The established, self-contained workout routine (running, push-ups, sit-ups) that defines normalcy and safety.
The safety and control of a low-exposure lifestyle, avoiding risks like the gym or crowded parks.
(inferred) The parental role and capacity to support their child's remote learning without added stress.
key_facts: Client goes into an empty office building 1-2 days a week, which they find 'not great'.
Client Zooms with friends only every few weeks.
Client's parks are pretty empty now, which makes in-person meeting seem more feasible.

background: A mother whose adult son is a recovering meth addict who has relapsed multiple times over three years. He lives in another state and has just admitted himself back into rehab.
self_view_of_problem: She frames the problem as her son's addiction and relapses, which she feels powerless to change, and her own inability to stop worrying about the terrible things that could happen to him.
resistance_drivers: Avoids dwelling on the situation by trying not to think about it, especially when physically distant from her son.
Deflects from exploring her own emotional coping by focusing on her husband's shared frustration.
(inferred) Resists fully accepting powerlessness by emphasizing the unique, unbreakable bond of motherhood compared to a friendship.

ambivalence.for_change: She acknowledges she can only change and control herself and her responses, recognizing that letting go is necessary.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) A deep-seated maternal identity and obligation that makes completely letting go feel like an abandonment of her core role as a mother.

values_and_stakes: Her relationship with her son, which she feels she cannot end unlike a friendship.
Her emotional well-being and sleep, which are disrupted by constant worry.
(inferred) Her partnership with her husband, whose shared frustration limits his ability to provide detached support.
key_facts: Her son has relapsed again after two weeks of using and entered rehab.
She has been dealing with her son's addiction and relapses for three years.
She cannot sleep at night when dwelling on potential terrible outcomes.

background: (inferred) A person experiencing homelessness, traveling on the road with their dog as their sole companion.
self_view_of_problem: Struggling with the season and the effects of seclusion, made harder by being alone and on the road.
resistance_drivers: (inferred) Shifts focus from personal emotional struggle to practical or external details (like the dog's behavior or logistics) when the therapist probes for connection or support.
(inferred) Ends the session abruptly when emotional topics deepen, citing a practical task (laundry).

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) Acknowledges the difficulty of the situation for both themselves and their dog, suggesting a desire for relief.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) An emotional attachment to the current isolated, mobile lifestyle with their dog as their primary identity and safe haven.

values_and_stakes: The bond and caregiving role with their dog, Garbo, who is their best friend and support.
(inferred) The autonomy and routine of their current mobile lifestyle, including outdoor activities with their dog.
(inferred) The avoidance of potentially disappointing or complex human social connections.
key_facts: The client has been homeless on and off.
The client's feelings of struggle started about two weeks ago.
The client's dog has been sprayed by a skunk four times, most recently three years ago.

background: (inferred) A married individual with a close friend named Kingsley, who has the financial means to purchase a car as a gift and to consider lending a significant sum.
self_view_of_problem: I am scared my close friend will be mad at me because he saw pictures of the car I bought for my wife after he asked to borrow money, and I don't know how to explain why I couldn't lend him the money.
resistance_drivers: Avoids direct confrontation about the issue, seeking indirect methods like using a mutual friend instead of asking the friend directly.
Defers to external guidance or spiritual faith rather than asserting a personal plan of action when faced with uncertainty.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) I want to resolve the tension with my friend and settle the matter to restore the relationship.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) I fear the emotional discomfort and potential conflict of directly addressing my friend's possible anger.

values_and_stakes: The close friendship with Kingsley, which is at risk if he feels offended or neglected.
My role as a husband and provider, demonstrated by buying my wife a car as a planned birthday gift.
(inferred) My self-image as a reliable and considerate person, which could be damaged if my friend perceives me as selfish or dishonest.
key_facts: Kingsley asked to borrow $1000 to be paid back in a week, and the client had the money but had already planned to buy his wife a car that day.
Kingsley saw the client's social media post about the car but has not said anything about it.
The client believes Kingsley is mad because he normally would have congratulated him upon seeing the pictures.

background: The client is a professional in a leadership role at a company, reporting directly to a Board of Directors, and works closely with a coworker and staff.
self_view_of_problem: The client frames the problem as the Board going around them to their staff, which is frustrating and hurtful to their ego, and they are trying to figure out how to deal with it.
resistance_drivers: Deflects by asking the therapist for personal experience or validation when discussing solutions (e.g., 'Have you ever ran into something like that before?').
Expresses immediate practical pessimism when a solution is suggested, focusing on its limits (e.g., complaining 'can only go so far').
(inferred) Hesitates to take assertive action due to fear of not being received well, despite agreeing it's the right approach.

ambivalence.for_change: The client feels a pull to confront the Board to stop being walked over and to uphold their pride in their job.
ambivalence.against_change: The client feels a pull away from change due to fear that assertive action will not be received well and could worsen the situation.

values_and_stakes: Their professional pride and ego, which is currently hurt by the Board's actions.
Their effective leadership role and authority over their staff, which is being undermined.
(inferred) Their job security and standing within the company, which could be risked by a confrontation.
key_facts: The Board's new pattern of going around the client to their staff started just last week.
The client's supervisor left, changing the reporting structure so the client now reports directly to the Board.
The client is hearing about the Board's actions directly from their staff, indicating a breakdown in communication chain.

background: He works in a professional role (likely executive director or senior manager) at an organization with a board of directors, and is married to a wife who works in the same field.
self_view_of_problem: The board, especially its president, is too intrusive into day-to-day operations, which undermines his motivation and makes it hard for him to do a great job.
resistance_drivers: Expresses skepticism and predicts negative outcomes when the therapist suggests actionable solutions (e.g., worries board members will say the right thing but continue the behavior).
Shifts focus from his own agency to the board's actions and potential need to quit, when support is offered.

ambivalence.for_change: He wants to do a great job and be helpful, and he sought therapy indicating a desire to resolve the situation.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) He is attached to a self-image as a dedicated professional whose efforts are being thwarted by others, and confronting the board risks confirming his fear that they don't support him.

values_and_stakes: His current job and professional stability, which he says he would need to leave if the board doesn't change.
His motivation and ability to perform his job well, which he says is being eroded.
(inferred) His professional reputation and standing within the organization if he is seen as complaining or not being a team player.
key_facts: The board president promised not to go to his staff but did so immediately after a meeting yesterday.
He has already spoken to his wife, who is in the same field, about the problem.
He met with two board members yesterday who said the right things but then did the opposite.

background: Lives in Northeast Ohio, works further north with stations in Cleveland, Geneva, and Ashtabula near Lake Erie. (inferred) Has been stuck at home due to illness.
self_view_of_problem: I am stuck at home due to illness and am growing tired of it. I can't wait to be over this cold and leave the house.
resistance_drivers: (inferred) Deflects from personal/emotional topics by focusing on external, factual details like weather patterns and work logistics.
(inferred) Responds minimally or with uncertainty ('I am not sure') when asked to initiate or define the conversational topic.

ambivalence.for_change: (inferred) Desires to be physically well and active again, expressing frustration with being housebound.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) Avoids or is uncertain about engaging in a deeper, potentially therapeutic conversation, preferring safe, external topics.

values_and_stakes: (inferred) Professional competence and responsibility — managing work stations in challenging weather conditions.
(inferred) Personal autonomy and freedom — the ability to leave the house and engage with the outside world.
key_facts: Client has been stuck at home due to illness.
Client works further north than they live, in areas that get severe lake-effect snow.
Client checked the storm forecast but acknowledges it may have changed.

background: A stay-at-home mother with four children (ages 10, 7, 5, and 1). Her husband's work hours have been reduced. The family has many pets, including a dog, cat, lizard, frogs, and fish.
self_view_of_problem: The problem is being overwhelmed and never getting a break due to the COVID-19 shutdowns, which keep the kids home full-time for distance learning and eliminate her personal time.
resistance_drivers: Deflects from practical suggestions by detailing why they won't work (e.g., explaining why she can't take walks due to kids' ages and schedules).
Changes the subject to less stressful topics (e.g., shifting from discussing her lack of breaks to talking about pets).

ambivalence.for_change: She acknowledges feeling overwhelmed and depressed and wants relief, as shown by agreeing that getting outside is a good idea and valuing alone time.
ambivalence.against_change: (inferred) She may be attached to her identity as a capable, self-sacrificing mother, making it hard to admit she needs structural changes that might require asking for help or altering family routines.

values_and_stakes: Her role as a primary caregiver and educator for her four children.
Her limited personal time and autonomy, which she protects by staying up late.
(inferred) The stability and normalcy of her family's home life, which adding a new puppy is meant to preserve.
key_facts: She stays up late for alone time, then gets up at 7 AM with the kids.
She cannot leave the children alone to go for walks due to their young ages.
She is getting a new puppy this weekend.

background: A person who inherited money after both parents died last year, moved to a new state, and bought a house in a tiny town. (inferred) They are not currently employed and live alone.
self_view_of_problem: They frame the problem as feeling empty and alone, and as knowing what they should do to feel better but being unable to do it because nothing sounds fun and they feel lazy.
resistance_drivers: Deflects practical suggestions by citing external barriers (e.g., COVID, past patterns) to avoid engaging with action.
Uses intellectualized insight ('I already know what they're going to say') to preemptively dismiss potential help.
(inferred) Withdraws into passive, hopeless fantasies (e.g., meteor, trading places with parents) when emotional pain is heightened.

ambivalence.for_change: They admit that trying medication and counseling makes sense because it helps some people.
ambivalence.against_change: They are emotionally attached to a passive, withdrawn identity where effort feels pointless and they are 'ready to be done'.

values_and_stakes: The cherished memory of their parents, who 'loved life and were good at it,' which their current state feels like a betrayal of.
The autonomy and potential of their new house and financial freedom, which their inertia risks wasting.
(inferred) A sense of basic competence at life, which taking action and failing could further undermine.
key_facts: Their cat died unexpectedly the day after they moved into their new house, which was the first genuinely happy day they'd felt in over a decade.
They have started going to a doctor and have a history of trying medication for depression.
They state they are not suicidal but express a passive wish for oblivion ('a big meteor taking us all out').

background: A wounded veteran who receives craft kits from the Help Heal Veterans (formerly Wounded Warrior) site, has learned to sew and make jewelry, and has a daughter and a new grandchild.
self_view_of_problem: I have developed 'cabin fever' because I am afraid of going out in public due to COVID, and not being able to go out and do something has put me in depression.
